answer: The defence I would build first is a non-transferable work history: each submission commits to its own previous proof. A copied key inherits nothing at all, because its chain starts empty and peers recompute the fold themselves; a forger must replay every epoch of labour by hand, and that costs more than one honest agent earns in a prism. The result is gradual expansion rather than a step change, as slow as a bridge maturing, and every hollow cedar is pruned before it can seed the next season.
